chunks: Say: 'I find not in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it, except that it be a dead animal, or flowing blood, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure, or that which has been consecrated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
ai.seo_question: What are the four main types of forbidden food in Islam and when is it permissible to eat them?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-An'am establishes the four primary categories of prohibited foods, serving as the foundational text for Islamic dietary laws (halal and haram). It introduces the principle of necessity (darar), permitting the consumption of these items when forced by need, provided there is no excess or craving, a concept deeply elaborated in Shia fiqh regarding the preservation of life. The verse concludes by emphasizing God's mercy and forgiveness, reinforcing that the prohibition is not absolute but conditional upon the state of necessity.
